title: Python Course
about_summary: Lessons teach the ideas. Tests you write and run right here prove you can use them.

about.heading: Code right here
about.body:
Every test has an editor. Type your program there: it saves as you type, so you can close the panel and come back later. **Run** runs your program and shows what it prints, and **Check my work** marks the whole test.

Everything runs on this computer with `python3`. Your code is also saved as files in `~/.config/waybar/learning-work/python`, if you ever want to open it in another editor.

about.heading: Lessons
about.body:
Each lesson explains one idea properly: what it is, why it works the way it does, and the mistakes people make with it. Examples show the syntax on a different problem from the test, so read them, then try your own version in a terminal.

Every lesson ends with three quick check questions. Get all three right to finish the lesson.

about.heading: Tests
about.body:
Each chapter ends with a test. The test page says exactly what your program must do and how it's checked, but never how to write it. Hints get stronger one at a time.

Tests feed your program input and check what it prints, so print exactly what's asked for, and don't pass a message to `input()`. Check as often as you like: each requirement gets a tick or a reason. Passing a chapter's test unlocks the next chapter.

about.heading: Daily review and your streak
about.body: Once you've finished a lesson, Daily review gives you five questions from lessons you've done, different every day. Finishing a lesson or a review, or checking a test, counts as practice for the day.

about.heading: Trying things out
about.body: Type `python3` in a terminal for the `>>>` prompt, where every line runs straight away. It's the fastest way to test an idea from a lesson. Press Ctrl+D to leave it.
